sections.heading: 1. Nights and days
lines: ① Wrists straight in bed (a splint is common).
② Keep your arms off and away from the pillow.
③ Break up gripping and scrolling every 30 min.
④ Wrists level on keyboard and mouse.

slides.heading: Get it checked if you notice

caption:
3am, and Mr Turtle is shaking pins and needles out of his hand again.

Tingling in the thumb, index and middle fingers, especially at night, is often linked to irritation of the median nerve at the wrist, known as carpal tunnel syndrome. Many people sleep with their wrists curled, which can add pressure.

Hybi's habits: keep the wrist straight overnight (a splint is a common first step), keep arms off the pillow, break up gripping and scrolling every 30 minutes, and keep wrists level at the desk.

Constant numbness, thumb weakness or dropping things are worth an assessment soon. Our Chatswood and Sydney CBD physios can help. Book online via the link in bio.
